text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Presidents of Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania launch common East African regional passport and flag.
- Family of murdered criminal lawyer Samuel Ndungi learns he was to sign two million shilling ($36,363) insurance policy a day before he died.
- Women's Political Caucus endorses opposition parliament member Charity Ngilu's candidacy for presidency.
- British immigration officials arrest Somali refugee travelling on forged Kenyan passport.
- Armed robbers shoot prominent businessman from coast region, snatching one million shillings from him.
- Nairobi Mayor Dick Waweru says residents will continue to get raw deal from city council because Local Authorities Act does not vest power in elected civic leaders.
- Motor mechanic and party activist Kuria Kanyingi is elected chairman of Kiambu branch of ruling KANU party.
- Members of parliament split over question of constitutional reforms or civil disobedience before next general election, due sometime this year.
- Kenya Consumers Organisation grinds to halt due to financial constraints.
